# Sirach Chapter 38 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_038_page_001.jpg

---

38:1 Give physicians the honor they deserve, because you need them — and because God made them.

38:2 Healing is a gift from the Most High; the physician receives recognition from those in power.

38:3 A physician's skill earns respect; even the great and powerful look up to them.

38:4 God created medicines from the earth. Don't be foolish enough to reject them.

38:5 Remember when water was made sweet by a piece of wood — God used that to show everyone his power.

38:6 He gave human beings the skill of healing so that he might be glorified through this remarkable work.

38:7 Through medicines, the physician takes away pain and cures the sick; the pharmacist prepares the remedies from the same source.

38:8 God's work of healing has no limit; it extends as health over the whole world.

38:9 My child, when you are sick — don't neglect yourself. Pray to the Lord, and he will bring healing.

38:10 Leave your wrongdoing behind. Make your hands do what is right. Cleanse your heart of every sin.

38:11 Offer incense and a grain offering. Make your sacrifice with oil, as generously as you can — offer it as though you still have life to give.

38:12 And then — give the physician his place. God created him too. Don't push him away; you need him.

38:13 There are times when your recovery depends entirely on the physician's hands,

38:14 because they too will pray to the Lord — asking him to grant success in their diagnosis and treatment, so that the patient may be restored to life.

38:15 The person who sins against their Maker — let them end up in the physician's hands.

38:16 My child, shed tears for those who have died. Begin your weeping like someone whose loss is great. Prepare the body properly; do not neglect the burial.

38:17 Let your mourning be heartfelt, your lamentation passionate. Mourn in proportion to the person's worth — a day or two, enough to be proper, then accept comfort.

38:18 Grief unchecked can kill; a sorrow-laden heart drains away your strength.

38:19 In times of disaster, sorrow takes root; and the hard life of the poor weighs the heart down.

38:20 Don't surrender your heart to grief. Shake it off. Remember: your time is coming too.

38:21 Don't forget — the dead cannot return. You cannot help them, and prolonged grief only hurts you.

38:22 "Think of my fate — you will share it. It was mine yesterday; it will be yours today."

38:23 When the dead is at rest, let the memory rest too. Find comfort when the spirit is gone.

38:24 A scholar needs leisure to grow in wisdom. You can't become wise if you're too busy.

38:25 Can the farmer who grips the goad and pushes the ox become wise? His whole world is his plow and his livestock. All his talk is about cattle.

38:26 He works at making his furrows straight. He's up at night worrying about fodder for his heifers.

38:27 The same is true of every craftsman and skilled worker — working day and night. Take the engraver of seals, focused on making a true likeness, determined to finish the work.

38:28 And the smith at his anvil, working iron — fire scorches his skin; he battles the furnace heat; the hammer pounds in his ears; his eyes are locked on the shape he's making. He pushes through to the end, determined to produce a fine piece.

38:29 And the potter sitting at the wheel, feet turning it steadily — anxious the whole time, calculating every piece.

38:30 He kneads the clay with his arms, treads it with his feet, concentrating on getting the glaze right, staying up to clean out the kiln.

38:31 All of them work with their hands, and each one is a master of their craft.

38:32 Without them, no city can exist. There's no settlement, no community, without these workers.

38:33 But you won't find them on the city council or in positions of public leadership. They don't sit as judges; they can't interpret laws or explain legal principles; they're not known for wise sayings.

38:34 But they hold the world together. And their prayer is offered in the work of their hands.
